best_for: Electronics students and analog designers who want a free SPICE simulator with schematic capture, especially for power circuits built around Analog Devices parts.

points.title: Free from the chip maker
points.text: Analog Devices gives LTspice away as freeware. It bundles schematic capture, the simulator and a waveform viewer, so one install covers drawing, running and plotting a circuit.

points.title: Mac and Windows now share a release
points.text: Version 26.0.0, dated December 1, 2025, was a parallel release on macOS and Windows and added support for ARM processors. Before that, the Mac edition ran on its own older version line.

points.title: The Mac build trails Windows
points.text: Windows is at 26.1.1 here while macOS is at 26.0.2. The MCP server for connecting third-party AI tools arrived in 26.1.0 in August 2026, so Mac users do not have it yet.

points.title: Mac needs macOS 14
points.text: The Mac installer listed here is a .pkg that needs macOS 14 or later. Users on older Macs have to look for an earlier release from another source.

points.title: Per-user or machine-wide on Windows
points.text: The Windows download is an x64 MSI that can install for the current user or for all users, which helps in labs and on machines without admin rights.

points.title: Convergence help is built in
points.text: 26.0.2 added an Improving Convergence document to the help FAQ, along with auto-scaling tiled windows and new shortcuts. 26.0.0 let you set loadstate, savestate and convergence reports inside the .tran directive.

points.title: Short version history
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 6 versions; macOS lists only the current release, so going back on a Mac needs another source.
